title: 1968 AHSME Problem 24
statement: A painting \(18''\times24''\) is to be placed into a wooden frame with the longer dimension vertical. The wood at the top and bottom is twice as wide as the wood on the sides. If the frame area equals that of the painting itself, the ratio of the smaller to the larger dimension of the framed painting is:

solutions.text:
The outside dimensions are \(18+2x\) and \(24+4x.\) Since the frame area equals the painting area, \((18+2x)(24+4x)=2(18)(24).\) This gives \(x^2+15x-54=0,\) so \(x=3.\) The dimensions are \(24\) and \(36,\) with ratio \(2:3.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Let each side strip have width \(x\), so each top strip has width \(2x\)
Set the outside area equal to twice \(18\cdot24\)
